articles.title: Post new funding rounds to Slack every morning with n8n
articles.excerpt: A Slack channel that posts three or four newly funded companies each morning gets read. A CRM view of the same companies usually does not. Here is that workflow in n8n. Four nodes, about fifteen minut…
articles.body: A Slack channel that posts three or four newly funded companies each morning gets read. A CRM view of the same companies usually does not. Here is that workflow in n8n. Four nodes, about fifteen minutes. The nodes 1. Schedule Trigger . Once a day, early. Pick a time before your reps start, so the list is waiting rather than arriving mid-call. 2. Datahyena. Fetch funding events with your filter. There is an n8n community node if you want the fields as a form, or use the HTTP Request node against the API directly. Either works. Set the filter tight. Stage, minimum amount, countries, industry. If you have not written your trigger down yet, do that first, because this node is where it lives. 3. Filter or Code. Optional, and worth adding once the basics work.

articles.title: How to Add an Authentic VHS Effect to Video in the Browser
articles.excerpt: If you've wanted that worn VHS look on a video without opening After Effects, here's what actually creates the effect and how to do it in the browser. Four things do most of the work: Tracking lines —…
articles.body: If you've wanted that worn VHS look on a video without opening After Effects, here's what actually creates the effect and how to do it in the browser. What makes footage look "VHS" Four things do most of the work: Tracking lines — horizontal distortion bands that drift vertically. Chroma shift — the red/blue channels offset from green, visible at edges. Grain and noise — analog signal hiss, brighter in dark areas. Date stamp — that blocky timestamp in the corner. Strip any of these and it stops reading as VHS. Add all four and even a clean clip looks dubbed. Browser approaches Canvas 2D — read each frame's pixels, shift the R and B channels a few pixels apart for chroma shift, overlay a noise pattern, and draw moving horizontal bands. Cheap and good enough for short clips.

articles.title: Your funding trigger is probably too broad
articles.excerpt: Most teams that run outbound off funding announcements define the trigger as "companies that raised". That is not a trigger. It is a firehose, and working it costs more time than doing nothing. The fi…
articles.body: Most teams that run outbound off funding announcements define the trigger as "companies that raised". That is not a trigger. It is a firehose, and working it costs more time than doing nothing. The fix takes about twenty minutes and it happens before you touch any tooling. Write the trigger as a filter someone else could run Four dimensions. Be specific on each one. Stage. A seed company and a Series D company buy completely differently. Seed has one person making the call and no procurement. Series D has a security review. Pick the stages that match how you actually sell. A $50k ACV product has no business chasing pre-seed. Amount. Round size is a rough proxy for what they can spend. Set a floor and be willing to raise it.

articles.title: ytscrape: One Python Interface for YouTube Data — No Browser, No API Key
articles.excerpt: Working with YouTube data from Python can quickly become complicated. You may need to search for videos, retrieve video metadata, inspect channels, collect comments and replies, download transcripts,…
articles.body: Working with YouTube data from Python can quickly become complicated. You may need to search for videos, retrieve video metadata, inspect channels, collect comments and replies, download transcripts, handle pagination, and work with different languages and regions. Usually, these tasks end up being split between different tools, APIs, browser automation, and custom scraping code. I wanted something simpler: One Python interface for collecting YouTube data. That's the idea behind ytscrape . ytscrape is a lightweight, typed Python library for collecting YouTube metadata, comments, transcripts, and search results through YouTube's internal HTTP API. No browser. No Selenium. No Playwright. No YouTube Data API key. Just Python and HTTP.

articles.title: On this day in space! Aug. 7, 1980: NASA's Viking 1 Mars orbiter shuts down 4 years into a 90-day mission
articles.excerpt: On Aug. 7, 1980, NASA's Viking 1 spacecraft orbiting Mars ended its epic and historic mission to the Red Planet. Here's why it mattered.
articles.body: On Aug. 7, 1980, NASA's Viking 1 spacecraft ended its epic and historic mission on the Red Planet. Viking 1 was the first spacecraft to successfully land on Mars . It was one of two Viking missions NASA launched in 1975 to go look for evidence of life on Mars . Each of the Viking missions were composed of an orbiter and a lander. Viking 1's orbiter took photos of the Martian surface that helped NASA decide where to drop the lander. Viking 1: The Historic First Mars Landing in Pictures After four years of orbiting Mars , the orbiter ran out of attitude-control propellant, so NASA had to shut it down. The lander continued its scientific observations for another three years before it lost contact with NASA in 1983.
